bottleneck: Motor neuroprostheses can decode movement intent, but restoring touch, proprioception, and graded force requires writing information back into the nervous system — and artificial sensory feedback remains crude. Stimulation-evoked sensations feel alien, lack natural timing and texture, and do not integrate with motor commands the way biological feedback does. Bidirectional interfaces are still mostly one-directional in practice, with the return path decades behind the decoding path in sophistication.
current_state: Intracortical microstimulation gives rough tactile percepts in trials, but naturalistic, high-resolution sensory feedback is unsolved. Patients describe sensations as unnatural buzzing or pressure.

sources.title: Toward Robust, Reproducible, and Widely Accessible Intracranial Language BCIs

title: Neuroprostheses lack natural sensory feedback
why_it_blocks: A prosthetic hand you cannot feel is a tool, not a limb. Without bidirectional feedback, fine manipulation and embodiment stay out of reach, and prostheses get abandoned.
